Episode 166. Traces of Calderan Snowfield (1)
The Eastern 5th region, Calderan Snowfield.
In this period, it was common for skilled adventurers or hardened warriors to lose their way and die in the Calderan Snowfield.
Of course, the party currently in the snowfield had no business of dying, but finding their way with just the map that Ronil had handed over was a difficult task.
If it hadn't been for Shuri. Shuri was, once again, doing a great job as the guide for the party.
"Kyahaha! Come here, Shuri. Let's have a peck with this sister. How can our Shuri be so smart? Could it be because you resemble your master?"
[Meow.]
As Shuri subtly pushed Sandra away, Zephyrin chuckled.
"Sister? That's funny, Miss Bio-Golem. Jin Runecandle's Cursed Jade Cat is an ancient creature that's at least a thousand years old."
"Oh dear, why is this trash starting a fight again?"
"A fight? I just found you amusing."
"Hedo, rip his mouth apart."
"I see you've been making inappropriate comments trusting your physical attractiveness. You should know that there are more monsters in this world than you think."

"Hmph, if you're so confident, why don't you try hitting me first? I guarantee that the moment you touch even a finger of mine, Hedo will definitely draw his sword. Then, of course, we'll fight until the end, and I think I know which side will win."
"Ah, really. How did I end up being treated like this. If it weren't for my master's order...."

"In the Sota Desert, you couldn't attack because of the things Jin stole, and now because of your master's orders. Being an Archduke of the Underworld seems nice. You always have an excuse even if you lose."
"Ha, okay. Then, Bio-Golem, you hit me first. I'll definitely kill you."
Unlike Zephyrin, Sandra tried to swing her fist immediately, but Hedo pulled her back, and she didn't reach Zephyrin.
Hedo sighed deeply, looking at Sandra flailing in his hand. Since the journey began, Sandra and Zephyrin had been constantly engaging in a battle of nerves.
Looking back, their vibes weren't so great when they first met in the Sota Desert either.
"Don't you think there's too little tension in enemy territory?"
Jin said.
"But Mr. Jin, he keeps getting on my nerves. You saw it just now, right? He started it."
"Is it a secret to Jin that you've been deliberately stepping on my heel the whole time we've been walking?"
"If either of you do it again, I'll leave you anywhere and go on my own. Without me, you all should have no trouble escaping from the Calderan Snowfield, right?"
Sandra and Zephyrin shut their mouths simultaneously.
'Power, good!'
'Damn it, if I tell my master that I was kicked out for fighting with a Bio-Golem, I'll be treated even worse...'
Sandra was silent because it was Jin's words, and Zephyrin because he knew it was not an empty threat.
As the two became quiet in an instant, Hedo was resentful of Jin, who had just now intervened.
The group moved quietly ahead.
It was at a very slow pace. Since Ronil's last visit to the snowfield, there had been knights steeped in chaos attacking Jin.
The moment they are detected, they would send a battalion from the Garden of Swords. In the worst case scenario, Rosa might even come herself.

It would take a significant amount of time for her to track from the Garden of Swords to Calderan Snowfield, but it was unpredictable if she used something like the Chaos Dragon or the Prophet's Cave used in Sota Desert.
'If Oul was here, we could have moved much faster, it's frustrating.'
Oul was currently unable to help Jin as he was tracking Yona's whereabouts.
In the nearly three years since the Glicek subjugation, Yona's rampage cycle was getting shorter and shorter.
Thinking of Yona made his heart ache.
'I have to use the purification device on my sister soon... I must find her before the erosion ends.'
According to the news Oul sent to Tikan a few days ago, she was not yet in the full erosion stage.
The Barmel Alliance couldn't find her better than No-name.
Jin found it a bit bitter that despite gaining such a great power, he was still not enough to fully protect his family and clan.
So he felt like he understood his father, Syron, a little bit.
They walked for three days, erasing their thoughts. Luckily, the group was able to pass through the snow-covered mountains without being detected by the knights on patrol.
However, they weren't able to get more additional information about Valeria during the move. There was nothing but snow and rock, a pale and dark sky that didn't distinguish between night and day.
"...It seems we've almost arrived."
A dead-end cliff cutting through the heart of the snowy mountains was visible in the distance.
Shuri pointed with her forefoot to one side of the cliff, which was not yet visible to the group, but that was where the cave was.
Jin returned Shuri to the Cursed Jade.
It was because of the feeling of Chaos. It had been like this continuously for the past three days, but especially near the cave, a thick Chaos was spreading.
"Hmm, I knew this would happen. While it's difficult to monitor the entire snowfield closely, they are definitely guarding the area near the cave where Hister disappeared."
"If you plan to continue entering, from here on out, I don't think we can avoid fighting. 12 Knights."
Zephyrin and Hedo said.
"We expected this problem anyway, we'll go in."
"You do realize that from here on out there are a lot of variables, right? Honestly, I'm not sure. Is it worth risking this much to save a survivor of Hester?"
"That's not for you to decide, Jephrin."
"You're such a tyrant. Of course, if Hester is in that cave, there's no need to worry. Honestly, Jin Kyung, don't you think that possibility is unlikely?"
"Hey! One of our companions disappeared over there. Whether there's a chance or not, shouldn't we at least go and check? Do demon slackers not have any camaraderie?"

"I hear some barking. Jin Kyung, what I'm suggesting is we look elsewhere, not the tundra. We missed Ronil Kyung and in my opinion, Runcan is the same. If they had caught them, they would have already started negotiations or threats."
As Jephrin said, there was no possibility of Valeria remaining in that cave.
However, Temar's tomb was always composed of 'subspaces'. In the Baolai of And Prairie, on the coast of Shcheron Kingdom, in the world of the Moeins, and in the Wontaramo forest.
Ronil had said that Valeria disappeared without a trace right in that cave.
'If there's a subspace leading to Temar's tomb inside that cave...'
Valeria reached the fifth tomb of Temar and escaped there.
Or it might not be an escape but a mandatory move triggered by the fulfillment of certain conditions.
"There can be a subspace, Jephrin. All the tombs of Temar I've encountered so far were like that."
"Are you suggesting that the survivors of Hester might have gone there? Now I get it a little bit. Why you haven't given up hope."
"Going from a tundra date to a subspace date! It's all romance!"
"And there was something I didn't understand from the start, why did you bring this living golem? It's not an energy sensor, always talking nonsense like this."
Jephrin was asking Hedoh, not Jin.
Hedoh didn't answer and wiped off the frost on his glasses.
"......12th generation, then the decision to enter is made. What's the plan?"
"I think Jephrin should take care of all the knights first."

Though the aura is strong, Jin thought that Jephrin could overwhelm all the knights near the cave. She may always lose or be tricked by Jin in one way or another, but she was undoubtedly one of the strongest in the world.
"And then it's obvious. Draw their attention until the real reinforcements arrive, right?"
"It's a rather simplistic approach."
"There's no other way. We can't assassinate all those people without a trace."
"Then what should I do?"
"Protect me while I look for traces of subspace in the cave."
"Well, I like that. I needed a target to vent my anger on anyway, because of some living golem."
"Jephrin."
"Yes?"
"I have a favor to ask."
Jin looked into Jephrin's eyes as he spoke.
Jephrin almost looked taken aback at his gaze. It was the first time she had seen this devil speak to her with such politeness.
"A favor...?"
"If possible, I'd like you to end the knights as painlessly as you can."
- Do you mean most of the knights remaining in the Sword Garden now didn't willingly pick up their arms, but were consumed by chaos?

- There would be some who did so willingly. But like you said, most probably didn't. Who would want to fight under such a monster? No matter how powerful the monster is. The knights of Runcan are, especially among them, very prideful.
Jin was recalling the conversation he had with Jordan while passing down the swords of their lineage.
Most of the knights now in the Coldran Tundra would have been turned into monsters of chaos against their will.
It was impossible to purify all of them. Judging from the size of their spiritual energy, they were nearly fully consumed.
Just as Jephrin was about to respond, Jin bowed his head to her once.
Jephrin then shrugged as if there was nothing she could do.
"......I will do as you wish. I'm not fond of the idea that it's for you, but it seems to be a more dignified thing to do."
"I appreciate it. I'll repay this favor."
"Should I start right away?"
"Yes."
"Signal me if anything unexpected happens. If I roar three times in a row, come out of the cave immediately and prepare to escape."
"Go get yourself killed. No! You can't die. Stay alive until we all get out of here, demon dragon! Make sure you keep your promise with Jin. Got it?"
As Jephrin transformed into her original form, she snorted in amusement.
[You just enjoy your solitary depressing date, living golem. Judging from my long experience, it seems like the Hester survivor that Jin is trying to save is more than just a comrade... Hehe.]
"What, what did you say!"
The knights in the tundra began to emit their spiritual energy in response to detecting Jephrin.
Sandra was pouring out curses at the sight of Jephrin taking flight.
